record.original_question: Given any generating set T of the symmetric group Sₙ, let Γ(Sₙ, T) be the corresponding Cayley graph. Determine whether there exists an absolute constant c such that the diameter of Γ(Sₙ, T) is always less than n^c.

evidence.quote: Prove (or disprove) that there exists a constant c such that for every n and for every set T of generators of the symmetric group Sₙ, the diameter of Γ(Sₙ, T) is less than nᶜ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite group $G$ and a generating set $T \subseteq G$, let $\Gamma(G,T)$ denote the Cayley graph whose vertex set is $G$ and whose edges connect $g$ to $gt$ for each $g \in G$ and $t \in T \cup T^{-1}$. The diameter of $\Gamma(G,T)$ is the maximum, over all pairs $g,h \in G$, of the length of a shortest path from $g$ to $h$ in this graph; equivalently, it is the smallest integer $d$ such that every element of $G$ can be written as a product of at most $d$ elements of $T \cup T^{-1}$.

Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Determine whether there exists an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that, for every positive integer $n$ and every generating set $T$ of $S_n$, the diameter of $\Gamma(S_n, T)$ is at most $n^c$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a special case of Babai's conjecture on diameters of Cayley graphs of finite simple groups, restricted here to the symmetric group. The best known general upper bound, due to Helfgott and Seress (Annals of Mathematics, 2014), is quasipolynomial: diam(Γ(S_n,T)) ≤ exp(O((log n)^4 log log n)). A polynomial bound n^c for arbitrary generating sets remains unproven, so the problem is still open in general, with partial results for restricted classes of generators (e.g., random generators, transpositions, bounded-rank Lie type analogs).

status_evidence.title: On the diameter of permutation groups (Helfgott–Seress)
status_evidence.snippet: Quasipolynomial upper bound exp(O((log n)^4 log log n)) on the diameter of S_n and A_n with any generating set.
status_evidence.claim: Best general bound is quasipolynomial; polynomial bound (Babai's conjecture for S_n) remains open.

status_evidence.title: Babai's conjecture for high-rank classical groups with random generators
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work establishing Babai's conjecture in special cases, indicating the general conjecture (including for S_n with arbitrary generators) is still open.
status_evidence.claim: Babai's conjecture remains open in general; only special cases are known.
